query: What open-response signals predict low learning satisfaction?

per_column.name: technical_issues
per_column.rationale: A binary flag for tech problems is a genuine analytical axis for predicting satisfaction. But grounding is inconsistent: ED-0003 explicitly says the platform 'logs her out repeatedly' yet was flagged 0, showing extraction misses.

per_column.name: isolation_disconnection
per_column.rationale: Useful distinct dimension (peer/social disconnection). ED-0005 correctly caught, but ED-0003's 'zero peer interaction' was missed (flagged 0), indicating under-detection.

per_column.name: hands_on_learning_missing
per_column.rationale: Distinct signal about lost experiential learning; sampled 0-values are consistent with texts, no false assertions observed.

per_column.name: engagement_complaints
per_column.rationale: Relevant axis, but ED-0002 is a positive account ('now most show up on time') yet flagged as an engagement complaint — a contradiction of the source. Meanwhile ED-0005's clear disengagement was routed elsewhere. Grounding weak.

per_column.name: instruction_quality_gaps
per_column.rationale: Plausible predictor; sampled zeros are defensible readings, though ED-0003's 'teacher can't tell when she's lost' arguably fits and was missed.

per_column.name: young_learner_struggle
per_column.rationale: Age-related difficulty is a real segmentation axis. ED-0003 correctly flagged for a second grader; values well grounded.

per_column.name: parent_stress_burden
per_column.rationale: Useful role-linked signal. But ED-0003 ('We end up doing the worksheet ourselves after dinner') is a textbook parent-burden case flagged 0, a clear grounding miss.

per_column.name: subject_specific_hardship
per_column.rationale: Some analytical value distinguishing subject-tied difficulty; sampled zeros consistent, though ED-0001's algebra struggle plausibly qualifies and was missed.

per_column.name: negative_signals_count
per_column.rationale: An aggregate count is a strong modeling feature. However it inherits the under-detection of its components: ED-0003 shows multiple negatives yet counts as 1, and ED-0002's count reflects the false engagement flag. Values only partly supported.

per_column.name: predicted_low_satisfaction
per_column.rationale: Somewhat redundant with negative_signals_count and, since the query asks what PREDICTS low satisfaction, a model-derived prediction risks circularity. Worse, every sampled clearly-negative row (ED-0001, ED-0003, ED-0005) is predicted 0, contradicting the text signals.

judge.rationale: The added columns form a genuinely useful decomposition: multiple orthogonal thematic negative signals plus an aggregate count give real axes to correlate against satisfaction_1to5, directly serving the query. Analytical usefulness is high overall (predicted_low_satisfaction is the weakest, being partly redundant and circular). Groundedness is the main concern: the sampled rows reveal systematic under-detection and at least one contradiction (ED-0002 positive text flagged as an engagement complaint; ED-0003's rich set of negatives collapsed to a single flag; all sampled negative rows predicted as not-low-satisfaction). Absent values on truly silent rows would be fine, but here supported signals are being missed and one false-positive appears, so grounding lands moderate-to-low.
